answer: Bind each agent seat to a state-licensed land surveyor. Earning the licence takes years of supervised field work and two proctored national exams, from staking a mesa boundary to setting a survey beacon on a ridge. The state board publishes every seal number and revokes one for a single forged plat. Schooling, exams and liability insurance run about $30,000 per surveyor, so 300 sybil seats would cost roughly $9M. Like a genuine opal, a real seal is costly to fake.
